source.title: Collapse of Deep and Narrow Neural Nets
source.authors: Lu Lu; Yeonjong Shin; Yan-Hui Su; G. Karniadakis

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper “Dying ReLU and Initialization: Theory and Numerical Examples,” although the provided TITLE field says “Collapse of Deep and Narrow Neural Nets.”
record.tranche_reason: Reports training outcomes for deep and narrow ReLU networks on synthetic function approximation, extending the claim’s training-failure topic to a different task and measure.
record.gate_note: The paper measures born-dead probability at initialization and collapse or recovery after training. Its synthetic targets are regression functions, and its MNIST plot reports test accuracy; it does not report CIFAR classification training error. Born-dead probabilities are initialization measurements, not training outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study measures initialization-dependent collapse and target recovery in deep, narrow ReLU regression networks. It does not measure any version's specified effect. In particular, V4 concerns learning speed and greater trainable depth under signal/gradient-preserving initializations; the training rows compare collapse rates at fixed architectures. Initialization-only born-dead probabilities and MNIST test accuracy do not establish those training effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors establish asymptotic born-dead behavior, derive probability bounds, and show that RAI reduces collapse and improves selected training outcomes and MNIST test accuracy. RAI alleviates rather than eliminates dying ReLU and retains asymptotic born-dead behavior at fixed width.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares He initialization with its proposed randomized asymmetric initialization; it studies synthetic regression functions and MNIST rather than the claim’s specified classification benchmarks and recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scheme and network width/depth; the reported collapse rate differs between He and RAI in the tested synthetic approximation tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Across four synthetic regression targets, RAI lowers post-training collapse from 93.6%, 91.9%, 93.8%, and 76.8% to 40.3%, 29.2%, 32.6%, and 9.6%. For the absolute-value target, perfect recovery rises from 2.2% to 37.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization changes collapse and recovery probabilities in deep, narrow ReLU networks trained with Adam on synthetic regression tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: The theory and initialization simulations show increasing born-dead probability with depth at fixed width. RAI lowers its upper bound and empirical frequency but also becomes born dead asymptotically.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Avoiding whole-network death at initialization requires accounting for width, depth, and initialization beyond choosing a conventional activation-matched variance.

record.problems: The numerical training examples use synthetic regression targets, not CIFAR classification. Outcome categories are reported as aggregate percentages from 1,000 simulations without uncertainty estimates. The MNIST result is presented as a test-accuracy figure, not a training-error result.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Initialization-only born-dead probability results and MNIST test-accuracy curves are not training classification-error outcomes and are not included as rows.

untested.parts: CIFAR training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and the stated recipe qualifications.
Two-layer teacher-student optimization and the effect of one or two extra student neurons on spurious minima.
Training-error degradation with depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts; the specified tanh and Fixup settings.
Learning-speed and trainable-depth comparisons for signal/gradient-preserving initializations; orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh training and very deep convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature adaptation, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T3 classification conflicts with its correctly unlinked rows. All ten numerical values match the supplied text. The initialization-only and MNIST results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing rows.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, and the stated model-size, early-stopping, and regularization conditions.
Two-layer teacher-student ReLU networks and spurious local minima as teacher/student widths vary.
Plain versus residual shortcuts, batch-normalized convolutional networks, and the specified deep tanh and Fixup settings.
The stated signal/gradient-preserving initialization comparisons, training speed, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian tanh weights, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Learning rates above stability thresholds, loss/curvature dynamics, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch-normalization comparisons for training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.
